coverage.assessment: The sequence from refusal to the 'superfluous' note to the reply is intact. Russell's 'leap to his opponent's ground' is unprepared because the Minister's political-power argument was cut. The Delane 'score' motive was thinned by the revision.

The Milnes scene's entrances, the embrace and Delane's eye are clear. The revision leaves 'the secretaries' without introduction next to 'If the Minister had no secretaries'. 'The notes' has no antecedent.
There is little speech. The unspoken 'You come next!', the three-point gloss and Gladstone's attributed remark with its added clause are correctly framed.
The revision correctly fixes 'suspicious' to 'felt any suspicion about'. Both drafts add 'nominal owner' to Bravay, an assertion that is not in Russell's letter. The checked dates are correct.
The 1863 judgment and the later retrospect remain distinct: 'in after life', the 1889 biography, 'forty years after'. The revelation is not premature. 'This was only the idea of a boy' is kept.
The revision trimmed several distinctive sentences: the stars, the cost that ruined, 'never got beyond 1815', and the 'Had the Minister known' irony. The periodic long sentences are often shortened.
The reversal still works. It is weaker because the secretary's certainty is cut: one of 'half a dozen persons', 'exploited' for family fortunes, and the incomparable education.
Both dependencies are intact. The Times leader appears in 010.revision. The Gotha letter is shown in 012.revision and only referenced here.

strengths: All eight verbatim lines survive. The 'one or two' setup sits immediately before 'not one of the two'.
The revision corrects the first draft's inverted gloss to 'what no one else in Europe or America felt any suspicion about'.
The tardy-notice irony is kept: the note arrives at three o'clock on 5 September, 'after the "superfluous" declaration of war had been sent'.
The full three-point gloss and 'The war was Russell's war--Adams only accepted it' preserve the secretary's reading.
The Turkish punchline survives in the Bravay paraphrase.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's spine: the Minister's practical stance, the mask image, the July 1863 climax, the Milnes embrace, the 'this is war' gloss, the 8 September reply, the 1889 reversal, the Bravay/Turks comedy and the Gladstone punchline. All eight verbatim lines survive. It also fixes the first draft's inverted 'doubted' gloss and its dangling Congress reference. Most remaining problems are small residues. Russell's 'leap to his opponent's ground' lacks the Minister's ground. The Delane 'thought'/'score' is less anchored. The 'secretaries' and 'notes' lack antecedents. A gloss calls Bravay the 'nominal' owner. The revision also cut several voice-bearing sentences, including the stars and cost lines, Russell's congenital 1815 senility, and the secretary's overconfidence. None of these is a blocker.
